ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Both B cells and T cells are required for an antibody response.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are four groups of irradiated recipient mice, and irradiation is used to remove the original lymphocytes. Subsequently, different cell populations are respectively reconstituted: the first group is not transferred with any cells, and the measured antibody response to the T-dependent antigen (sheep red blood cells) is "--"; the second group is transferred only with bone marrow cells, and the antibody response is "--"; the third group is transferred only with thymus cells, and the antibody response is "--"; the fourth group is transferred with bone marrow cells and thymus cells at the same time, and the antibody response is "++". Reasoning: The recipient mice have been irradiated and basically lack their own lymphocytes, therefore the observed antibody response depends on the transferred cell populations. Bone marrow cells alone cannot produce an antibody response, and thymus cells alone also cannot produce an antibody response; only when bone marrow cells and thymus cells are present at the same time does a strong antibody response appear. Bone marrow-derived cells provide B cells, and thymus-derived cells provide T cells. From this it can be known that, when producing an antibody response to this T-dependent antigen, both B cells and T cells are necessary, and the presence of either type of cell alone is not sufficient to induce an effective antibody response.

You irradiated recipients first to ablate (get rid of) existing lymphocytes, then transferred defined cell populations from donors of same genetic background. The result is shown in the figure. What does this experiment tell us?
raw_record.standard_answer: Both B cells and T cells are required for an antibody response.

method.method_draft: First describe the figure: irradiated mice are reconstituted with different donor cell populations, and antibody response to a T-dependent antigen is measured. Compare the outcomes: no cells gives no response, bone marrow cells alone gives no response, thymus cells alone gives no response, but bone marrow plus thymus cells gives a strong response. Since the only successful condition contains both bone marrow-derived B-lineage cells and thymus-derived T cells, infer that neither population alone is sufficient; both B cells and T cells are required for the antibody response.

图像描述：图中有四组被照射的受体小鼠，照射用于去除原有淋巴细胞。随后分别重建不同细胞群：第一组不转入任何细胞，测得对T依赖性抗原（绵羊红细胞）的抗体反应为“--”；第二组只转入骨髓细胞，抗体反应为“--”；第三组只转入胸腺细胞，抗体反应为“--”；第四组同时转入骨髓细胞和胸腺细胞，抗体反应为“++”。
推理：受体小鼠已被照射，基本缺乏自身淋巴细胞，因此观察到的抗体反应取决于转入的细胞群。骨髓细胞单独不能产生抗体反应，胸腺细胞单独也不能产生抗体反应；只有骨髓细胞和胸腺细胞同时存在时才出现强抗体反应。骨髓来源细胞提供B细胞，胸腺来源细胞提供T细胞。由此可知，对这种T依赖性抗原产生抗体反应时，B细胞和T细胞都必需，任何一类细胞单独存在都不足以诱导有效抗体反应。

method.method_draft: Treat the experiment as a loss-and-rescue design. The irradiated-only group establishes that ablated mice cannot mount the antibody response. Adding bone marrow cells alone fails, so B-lineage/antibody-producing cells without thymus-derived T-cell help are not enough. Adding thymus cells alone also fails, so T cells without B cells are not enough. Full rescue occurs only when both bone marrow and thymus cells are transferred. Therefore the experiment demonstrates cooperative requirement: both B cells and T cells are needed to generate the antibody response to the T-dependent antigen.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有四组被照射的受体小鼠。重建方式分别是：不转入细胞、只转入骨髓细胞、只转入胸腺细胞、同时转入骨髓细胞和胸腺细胞。下方测量的是受体小鼠对T依赖性抗原，即绵羊红细胞，产生抗体应答的能力。前三组结果均标为“--”，表示没有抗体应答；只有同时接受骨髓细胞和胸腺细胞的一组标为“++”，表示抗体应答恢复。
推理：这是一个缺失-救援实验。照射后不补充细胞的小鼠不能产生抗体应答，说明去除淋巴细胞会消除该应答。只补充骨髓细胞仍无应答，说明B细胞/抗体产生细胞谱系单独不足。只补充胸腺细胞也无应答，说明T细胞单独不足。只有骨髓细胞和胸腺细胞共同转入时抗体应答被救援，因此该T依赖性抗原的抗体应答需要B细胞和T细胞协同参与。
